entrypoints.summary: An attacker-deployed module with invalid claims reaches extract_claims while claims are decoded; the report also shows a fuzz target passing arbitrary byte slices directly to wascap::wasm::extract_claims.

affected_components.role: A parser-produced custom-section range is used to slice the original input buffer while building a wasm_encoder::RawSection.

causal_paths.kind: untrusted binary input to unchecked slice

code_slices.fixed: if let Some((id, range)) = payload.as_section() { if range.end <= buf.len() { wasm_encoder::RawSection { id, data: &buf[range] }.append_to(&mut output); } else { return Err(errors::new(ErrorKind::InvalidCapability)); } }
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report identifies this as wascap/src/wasm.rs#L161-L167 in the strip_custom_section path used by extract_claims.
code_slices.vulnerable: if let Some((id, range)) = payload.as_section() { wasm_encoder::RawSection { id, data: &buf[range] }.append_to(&mut output); }

negative_controls: A range whose end is within buf proceeds through the guarded slice path.
An out-of-buffer range on the documented fixed path returns InvalidCapability rather than slicing.
observability.positive_marker: extract_claims panics and the assessed deployment crashes the associated Elixir process.

preconditions: The attacker can deploy a module with invalid claims to the assessed claims-decoding path.
The vulnerable implementation processes the supplied module through extract_claims.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Malformed WASM/module byte sequence that yields an out-of-buffer custom-section range; exact bytes are not provided.
trigger_steps.summary: Deploy a module carrying invalid claims so claim decoding invokes extract_claims and reaches a parser-provided range outside the backing buffer.

mitigations.concept: validate parser-derived section range against backing buffer length

relation_candidates.rationale: The finding's exploit scenario supplies invalid module claims, while the shown harness supplies arbitrary bytes to extract_claims, whose vulnerable path slices the input using a parser-provided range.
The report states that a range outside the buffer causes the unchecked slice path to panic.
For wasmCloud-otp, the report says Rustler gracefully handles the panic as an isolated Elixir-process crash.

relation_candidates.dst: validate parser-derived section range against backing buffer length
relation_candidates.rationale: The documented repair checks range.end <= buf.len() before slicing and returns an error otherwise.

impact.affected_asset: The Elixir process handling the claims-decoding request; the report states Rustler gracefully contains the panic rather than asserting VM-wide failure.
impact.attacker_capability: An attacker able to deploy a module with invalid claims can cause extract_claims to panic during claim decoding.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through an isolated Elixir-process crash in the assessed deployment.

causal_trace.summary: A crafted module supplies invalid claims / arbitrary WASM bytes to the extract_claims input path.
payload.as_section() supplies an id and range, but the vulnerable path does not establish that the range end is within the original buf before use.
strip_custom_section constructs RawSection with data taken through the Rust slice expression &buf[range].
A range outside the buffer causes extract_claims to panic; in the assessed wasmCloud-otp deployment Rustler handles this as an isolated Elixir-process crash.

failure.operation: Rust slice indexing of the original input buffer using an unchecked parser-derived section range (&buf[range])

primary_invariant.statement: Before slicing buf with a parser-provided section range, range.end must be less than or equal to buf.len().
primary_invariant.violated_because: The vulnerable RawSection construction slices buf[range] without the documented range.end <= buf.len() guard.

raw_refs.role: canonical public security-assessment finding, vulnerable code, fuzz harness, and proposed fix

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report embeds the vulnerable slice, a direct cargo-fuzz harness, the scenario, and a bounds-check fix. It does not bundle a minimized crashing input, an execution log, or a version-pinned pre-fix repository snapshot; the fuzz harness establishes an oracle contract and is not treated as a recorded passing test result. The remote deployment interface and exact affected release range are not specified by the inspected finding.

remediation.invariant_restored: The documented fix performs range.end <= buf.len() before &buf[range] and returns InvalidCapability when the check fails.
mitigation_classes: return an error instead of performing an out-of-range slice

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Provide a deployable module whose claims decode into a section range outside the supplied byte buffer.
data_structure_invariants: A custom-section range returned by payload.as_section() must remain within the backing buf before buf[range] is evaluated.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The attacker-controlled input must lead parsing to return a range that is not within buf; the report gives no minimized byte sequence.
numeric_domains.name: section range end and input length

state_context.state_machine: Claims decoding obtains a custom-section descriptor and either appends its raw input bytes to output or, after the documented fix, rejects an invalid range with InvalidCapability.

oracle.channel: cargo-fuzz harness invoking wascap::wasm::extract_claims on arbitrary byte slices
oracle.expected_negative: With the documented guard, an out-of-buffer range returns InvalidCapability rather than reaching &buf[range].
oracle.expected_positive: A malformed byte sequence that produces a parser section range outside buf causes the pre-fix slice path to panic.
